conventions.convention: Coefficients are F₂; U has degree −2; CF⁻ is generated by [x,i] with i<0, and CF⁺ is its quotient from CF∞. The standard S³ generator [x₀,0] has degree zero.
The correction term is the minimum grading of a nonzero homogeneous element in im(HF∞→HF⁺). Plus-tower elements are U-torsion and infinitely U-divisible; U-nontorsion is not required.
A fixed Spin-c cobordism map has degree (c₁²−2χ−3σ)/4, with the Chern square evaluated through the rational intersection form.
L(p,1) means positive p-surgery on the unknot. Labels are represented by 0≤i<p, with characteristic value 2i−p; conjugation sends i to p−i modulo p. Opposite orientation negates correction terms.
Spin-c lift classes use the actual H² torsor action by line bundles, rather than classification by determinant classes. Boundary restriction is equivariant for restriction in H².

The cohomological linking form is defined using the Q/Z coefficient Bockstein and cup evaluation. Its comparison with chain linking allows a global orientation sign, which leaves annihilator subgroups unchanged.

The slice-cover statements assume AC and smooth proper slice disks, use positive-meridian mod-two monodromy, and assert no corresponding smooth correction-term conclusion from merely locally flat topological disks.

load_bearing.statement: For every closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere and Spin-c structure, the standard HF∞ and HF⁺ groups are independent up to grading-preserving isomorphism; the infinity image is a graded plus tower with an invariant least grading, normalized to zero for S³.
The correction term d(Y,t) is the minimum absolute grading of a nonzero homogeneous element in im(HF∞(Y,t)→HF⁺(Y,t)).

Assume AC. For a compact connected oriented smooth rational homology four-ball B with connected rational homology sphere boundary Y, the extending boundary Spin-c structures form one affine coset of M=im(H²(B;Z)→H²(Y;Z)); the linking pairing is nonsingular, M=M⊥, and |M|²=|H₁(Y;Z)|.

For a smooth compact connected oriented rational homology four-ball and an extending boundary Spin-c structure, puncturing gives degree-zero infinity isomorphisms in both cobordism directions; the plus comparisons give d(Y,t)≥0 and d(Y,t)≤0.
If a boundary Spin-c structure t on the oriented rational homology sphere boundary Y of a smooth compact connected oriented rational homology four-ball B extends over B, then d(Y,t)=0.

Assume AC. The connected double cover of B⁴ branched along a smooth properly embedded slice disk D is a rational homology four-ball with oriented boundary Σ₂(∂D) in the positive-meridian convention.

Assume AC. The complement of the interior of a closed tubular disk bundle of the nonsingular conic [s:t]↦[s²:st:t²] in CP² is a smooth compact rational homology four-ball; orient it so its boundary is L(4,1) in the stated convention.

seams_checked.note: The positive-meridian definition supplies the boundary-cover convention. The inverse-matrix surgery lemma supplies H₁(L(4,1))=Z/4; the example does not infer extending Spin-c labels from that homology calculation.

The smooth proper-surface and collar conventions agree with the smooth slice-disk use. The consumer explicitly excludes merely locally flat topological disks and invokes no concordance group-law conclusion.

The closed-manifold hat and analytic suppliers are used within their stated scopes. Generic minus/infinity/plus invariance, absolute grading and fixed-Spin-c cobordism properties are supplied separately; they are not inferred from grid invariance for knots in S³.

The lens-space definition uses positive p-surgery, matching the formula and the conic boundary calculation. The +4-framed unknot diagram agrees with the construction. The formula and vanishing conclusion also match [Ozsváth–Szabó, Proposition 4.8 and Proposition 9.9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0110170v1).
